subject.title: Codex-OAuth models fail over incorrectly — sibling model with healthy per-model quota still drops to non-codex fallback

question: For Codex OAuth sibling-model failover, should OpenClaw keep Codex models on the app-server and repair the model-scoped cooldown/app-server path, or add direct-runtime Codex Harmony tool-call support as a supported fallback?
rationale: Both directions can plausibly solve part of the report, but they change runtime ownership, provider routing, and tool-call parsing behavior in compatibility-sensitive auth/provider code.

options.title: Land scoped cooldown first
options.body: Finish #99810 or an equivalent narrow fix so one model's subscription_limit does not suspend sibling models, while keeping app-server as the Codex default pending live app-server proof.

options.title: Investigate app-server upstream
options.body: Collect maintainer-owned live traces for the suspected Codex websocket/rate-limit context problem before changing OpenClaw's runtime routing.

options.title: Build direct Harmony adapter
options.body: Add Codex Harmony tool-call extraction to the direct Responses runtime and prove real Codex tool calls before allowing direct Codex OAuth routing.

recommendation.title: Land scoped cooldown first
recommendation.body: Finish #99810 or an equivalent narrow fix so one model's subscription_limit does not suspend sibling models, while keeping app-server as the Codex default pending live app-server proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest overlap across OpenAI/Codex provider identity, fallback/model support, and the direct runtime surface.
